root_cause.text: In the BPF per-cpu hashtab path, `pcpu_init_value()` wrongly assumed source values were 8-byte padded and used `copy_map_value_long()`, which rounds small `value_size` copies up to 8 bytes even when the actual source buffer (such as `BPF_MAP_TYPE_CGROUP_STORAGE`) is only the exact unrounded size.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says "`pcpu_init_value` assumes that all sources are rounded up to 8 bytes" and that this fails for sources like `CGROUP_STORAGE` or `skb->data`, causing OOB when "the source has only 4 bytes while the copy size(4) is rounded up to 8"; the patch fixes this by replacing `copy_map_value_long()` with `copy_map_value()` in `kernel/bpf/hashtab.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the correct generic value copy helper when initializing the current CPU's per-CPU hash map entry to avoid improper value initialization.
intent_record.what: The call inside pcpu_init_value() for the current CPU case was changed from copy_map_value_long(&htab->map, per_cpu_ptr(pptr, cpu), value) to copy_map_value(&htab->map, per_cpu_ptr(pptr, cpu), value), while the surrounding loop and zero_map_value() handling for other CPUs remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, initialization of the current CPU's per-CPU map value now uses the generic map value copy helper instead of the long-only variant, causing the value to be copied according to the map's actual value semantics and avoiding incorrect initialization when the value is not meant to be handled by the specialized long copy path.

grouping_result.intent: Use the correct generic value copy helper when initializing the current CPU's per-CPU hash map entry to avoid improper value initialization.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it replaces the per-CPU hash map initialization copy path with the generic helper instead of the long/8-byte-rounded copy helper, preventing incorrect copying of unpadded source values.

candidates.rationale: This statement is the direct root cause: it uses the long-copy helper during per-CPU hash value initialization, which rounds small value_size copies up to 8 bytes and can read past the end of an unpadded source buffer.

vuln_statements.explanation: This per-CPU hash table initialization statement uses copy_map_value_long(), which assumes 8-byte padded source values and rounds small value_size copies up to 8 bytes. When the source buffer is only the exact unrounded size, this can read past the end of the source during initialization.

Author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi <memxor@gmail.com>

    elements.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant vulnerable logic is shown directly in `pcpu_init_value()`, so the snippet is sufficient. In this commit, the `!onallcpus` path does `copy_map_value_long(&htab->map, per_cpu_ptr(pptr, cpu), value);` for the current CPU. Per the root cause, the bug is that `pcpu_init_value()` assumes the source buffer is 8-byte padded and uses `copy_map_value_long()`, which rounds small `value_size` copies up to 8 bytes. That exact construct is present here in `pcpu_init_value()`. The comment says this path is used when `onallcpus=false`, and the root cause specifically notes such sources may be exact-size buffers (e.g. cgroup storage), so rounded-up copying can over-read the source. There is no protective handling here to use an exact-size copy for the source buffer in this path; instead it still uses the rounded copy helper. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present (`has_bug=true`) and the fix is not yet present (`is_fixed=false`).

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function bodies are sufficient to judge the relevant copy behavior for the newly introduced per-cpu hash path. In this commit, per-cpu element initialization is done in `alloc_htab_elem(..., bool percpu)`. In the percpu branch, the code explicitly rounds the allocation size up — `size = round_up(size, 8);` and `pptr = __alloc_percpu_gfp(size, 8, ...)` — but when initializing from the caller's source buffer it copies only the real value length: `memcpy(this_cpu_ptr(pptr), value, htab->map.value_size);`. Likewise, in `htab_percpu_map_update_elem()` the in-place update also uses `memcpy(..., value, htab->map.value_size);`. The root cause described is use of `pcpu_init_value()` / `copy_map_value_long()` that rounds small copies up to 8 bytes and can over-read an exact-sized source buffer. That vulnerable construct is not present in this commit snippet; the code uses plain `memcpy` with the exact `value_size` instead. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent (`has_bug=false`). At the same time, this commit does not show the later specific fix of replacing a buggy `copy_map_value_long()`-based path, because that buggy path was never introduced here; so this version should not be marked as already containing that fix (`is_fixed=false`).
